author: Sonja Kelley
description: The No-cover SOP as a command: fail the build when a fixed or floating element covers readable text or a tappable control.
name: no-cover

scripts.test: npm run test:fixture && npm run test:clean && npm run test:exempt && npm run test:odd && npm run test:odd-narrow && npm run test:shadow
scripts.test:exempt: node ./bin/no-cover.mjs ./test/fixture-exempt.html --widths 360,1280; test $? -eq 0 && echo 'fixture-exempt: correctly PASSED (deliberate in-your-face banner, exempt)'
scripts.test:fixture: node ./bin/no-cover.mjs ./test/fixture.html --widths 360,1280; test $? -eq 1 && echo 'fixture: correctly FAILED (banner covers the million-dollar button)'
scripts.test:odd: node ./bin/no-cover.mjs ./test/fixture-odd.html; test $? -eq 1 && echo 'fixture-odd: correctly FAILED (banner only covers the button at 412px — the default widths catch it)'
scripts.test:odd-narrow: node ./bin/no-cover.mjs ./test/fixture-odd.html --widths 360,1280; test $? -eq 0 && echo 'fixture-odd narrow: correctly PASSED at 360/1280 — the cover only exists at 412px, which is why the default widths are broad'
scripts.test:shadow: node ./bin/no-cover.mjs ./test/fixture-shadow.html --widths 360,1280; test $? -eq 1 && echo 'fixture-shadow: correctly FAILED (banner hidden inside a web component shadow root still caught)'
